title: A Process for Wisely Deciding How to Educate Your Children
author: Tim Challies
summary: Challies provides a five-question framework for educational decision-making: identifying possible options, determining actual options given constraints, seeking wise counsel, testing decisions against Scripture and conscience, and finally choosing the best option for your family. He emphasizes that parents bear responsibility for education but that no single option is universally superior; what matters is the process by which the decision is made and how children are supported afterward.
points: Educational decisions should be made by parents according to conscience informed by Scripture, not by church authorities or social media advocates. The five-question process filters options first by constraint, then by conscience, then by informed judgment. Wise counsel should come from people who have chosen each option, from young adults who have completed different systems, and from trusted Christian advisors. What's most important is not which option you choose but how you make the decision and how you support your children through it. No single educational approach produces universally superior outcomes; all three main options (public, Christian, homeschool) have produced both faithful and wayward young adults.
quotes: This is a matter for parents to decide, not the wider church, not social media, and not advocates of any particular position.
The best decisions flow from a biblically guided mind and a well-informed conscience.
No educational option can allow the parents to be uninvolved.
We can best serve our brothers and sisters in the Lord by speaking calmly, respectfully, and without hyperbole.
